question: Under competitive assets market condition, the price of a bond must always be ______________ to its present value in equilibrium.
solution:
The correct answer is __**equal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under competitive market conditions, the price of a bond in equilibrium is always **equal to its present value**, which is calculated based on discounted future cash flows.
 
• The present value is determined using the **market interest rate**, also referred to as the discount rate.
 
• The equilibrium condition ensures that the bond price reflects its intrinsic value, preventing **arbitrage opportunities**.
 
• If the bond price deviates from its present value, market forces will adjust the price to restore equilibrium.
 
• This principle is rooted in the concept of **efficient markets**, where asset prices fully reflect all available information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bond Pricing:**

 
 
• Bonds are priced based on their future cash flows, including periodic coupon payments and the principal repayment at maturity.
 
• The present value of these cash flows is calculated using the prevailing **market interest rate**.
 
• A higher market interest rate results in a lower present value (and price), while a lower interest rate increases the present value.
 
 
 
• **Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH):**
 
 
• This theory states that asset prices reflect all available information, ensuring no persistent arbitrage opportunities.
 
• Bond prices under competitive market conditions align with their intrinsic value, supporting EMH.
 
 
 
• **Discount Rate:**
 
 
• The discount rate is the interest rate used to calculate the present value of future cash flows.
 
• It reflects the opportunity cost of capital and market risk.
 
 
 
• **Arbitrage:**
 
 
• Arbitrage refers to the practice of profiting from price discrepancies in different markets.
 
• In competitive markets, bond prices adjust quickly to eliminate arbitrage opportunities.
